text:
Sonal: Heads-up — nightly-eval spike for long-context code promptset. pass_rate dropped to 84.5% on redwood-model-0.9q (int4 dynamic). Baseline was 99.2% yesterday. Repro + notes below.

Sonal: Repro (short):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-model-0.9q","prompt":"<file1>\n```python\ndef foo():\n  return bar\n```\n<file2> ... (long context)" ,"max_tokens":256}'
```

Evan: Ack — see eval dashboard snapshot: https://dash.internal/redwood/nightly/171999 — failing buckets are long_code_fences and file-merge cases.

Jia: I saw tokenizer v2.1 landed in onboarding yesterday (PR #452) that canonicalizes code-fence markers into a single token ` ``` ` instead of three backticks. Could be interaction with quant.

Cris: Checked quant calibration logs for v0.9q: observed embedding L2 norm shift on the new fence token (avg norm -24%). Dynamic clipping threshold got aggressive when we used minmax per-channel.

qa-bot: Attached sample ids: EVAL-2026-0319-001..005 (examples show hallucinated filler code inserted mid-file). Link: https://ci.redwood/evals/171999/examples

Sonal: Preliminary root-cause hypothesis: tokenizer change merged fence into a single token. The int4 quantized embedding for that token diverges from fp16 variant, and with long contexts the KV cache alignment amplifies the misinterpretation => LM injects spurious code blocks/hallucinations.

Evan: Proposed mitigations (short-term -> medium):
  1) Immediate rollback: route long-context requests (>=1024 tokens) to fp16 variant (redwood-model-0.9_fp16) until fix.
  2) Canary: create `int4-code-canary` at 2.5% traffic but explicitly exclude long-context endpoints.
  3) CI gating: add nightly gate that requires long_code_promptset pass_rate >= 98% before promoting any quant build.
  4) Tokenizer fix: revert canonicalization of code-fence to preserve three backticks as separate tokens OR add explicit token mapping + unit tests.
  5) Recalibrate quant with relaxed clipping on the new token embedding.

Jia: I'll open a PR to revert/fix tokenizer normalization and add a multi-file code-context unit test. Target: EOD today. @Evan please add test to gating.

Cris: I'll run recalibration with per-layer scale adjustment (less aggressive clipping) and produce a canary image by EOD. Running microbench now. ETA ~4h.

deploy-bot: Rollout ticket RL-7892 created for rollback of redwood-model-0.9q on Dedicated. Scheduled start in 15m (rolling to fp16 for long-context routes).

Sonal: Action owners / timeline: Jia -> tokenizer PR + tests (EOD). Cris -> recalibration + canary build (EOD). Evan -> CI gating rule + canary policy (ASAP). I (Sonal) will run the rollback and own comms to SEs/customers. If canary fails we fully revert quant variant.

Evan: Gating snippet (draft): `gates.long_code_pass_rate >= 0.98 && metrics.regression_count == 0` — will add to nightly-eval pipeline.

mscott: FYI I'll ping Dedicated/Sales channels once rollback starts so customers know latency/perf tradeoffs.

Sonal: Quick temporary server-side fallback plan: if request.context_length >= 1024 then set model_override=redwood-model-0.9_fp16. Evan pls add to routing policy.

Evan: Added routing rule draft to infra repo, PR sent.

Cris: Running local reproducer w/ original tokenizer vs v2.1 + int4 calib. Early signs: fixing clipping restores sanity for the fence token.

Sonal: Good. After rollout we'll run targeted nightlies and a small canary (2.5%) for general traffic, but keep long-context excluded until we validate. Postmortem + root-cause writeup after we confirm. :+1:
